text:
Three red flags Google watches for on your Business Profile:

1. Extra words stuffed into your business name.
2. Reviews you paid for, swapped for, or wrote yourself.
3. A PO box or virtual office as your address.

Any one of them can get your profile suspended.

Christmas hours go into Google Business Profiles over the next few weeks.

That's when wrong hours cost the most.

Google gives you four days to reject a suggested edit. Miss the email and Google can publish it anyway if your website backs it up.

Fix your website hours first.

Picture a cafe in Surry Hills. Forty five-star reviews in one week, all from accounts with no other reviews.

Then a notice goes up on the profile: fake reviews were removed.

Google can also block new reviews and hide the old ones for a set time.

(Busiest week they never had.)

A website with no Google Business Profile is a thousand flyers sitting in your glovebox.

Lovely flyers. Great font. Nobody sees them.

Someone searches "electrician near me" and gets a map. Three names, star ratings, a Call button.

The profile is free. Claim it first.

Ten electricians in Joondalup with keywords stuffed into their Google names.

So it must work.

The majority is ALWAYS wrong. About six months before they find out.

Google says extra words in your name could get your profile suspended.

https://gimsresults.com.au/post/google-business-profile-name

Most marketing problems I see are housekeeping.

Wrong hours. An old phone number. A special that ended in June.

Fix the boring stuff first. It costs nothing.

Then we can talk about the clever stuff. (There's less of it than you'd think.)
